ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Three one-inch squares are palced with their bases on a line. The center square is lifted out and rotated $ 45^\circ$, as shown. Then it is centered and lowered into its original location until it touches both of the adjoining squares. How many inches is the point $ B$ from the line on which the bases of the original squares were placed?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure shows three side-by-side one-inch squares, whose bottom sides are all on the same horizontal straight line; the middle square is marked with shading, and point B is near the upper side of the middle square. The arrow indicates that the middle square is taken out and rotated 45°. The right side shows the rotated gray square in the shape of a rhombus, centered and put back in the original middle position, and lowered until it touches the upper inner corners of the two adjacent squares on the left and right; point B is the highest vertex of the rotated rhombus. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, let the straight line where the bottom sides of the original three squares lie be y=0, and let the middle position be 1≤x≤2, so the center of the rotated square is on the line x=3/2. The upper inner corners of the left and right adjacent unit squares are respectively (1,1) and (2,1). Let the center of the rotated unit square be (3/2,c). After the unit square is rotated 45°, its diagonals are vertical and horizontal, and the half-diagonal length is r=√2/2. Therefore the bottom vertex is (3/2,c-r), and vertex B is (3/2,c+r). The left contact point (1,1) is on the lower-left side of the rhombus; this side has slope -1 and passes through the bottom vertex (3/2,c-r). Its equation satisfies y-(c-r)=-(x-3/2). Substitute (1,1): 1-(c-r)=-(1-3/2)=1/2, so c-r=1/2, that is, c=1/2+√2/2. Thus the height of point B is c+r=1/2+√2/2+√2/2=√2+1/2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the final diagram, take the original base line as y=0, the middle slot as 1≤x≤2, and the rotated square centered on x=3/2. The adjacent unit squares have their upper inner corners at (1,1) and (2,1), and the lowered diamond touches them there. Let the center of the rotated unit square be (3/2,c). Since the square has side 1 and is rotated 45°, its half-diagonal is r=√2/2, so its left/right/top/bottom vertices are horizontally or vertically r from the center, and its lower sides have slopes ±1. Put the point (1,1) on the lower-left side (or (2,1) on the lower-right side), solve for c, then add r to get the height of the top vertex B. This gives c=1/2+√2/2 and height(B)=c+√2/2=√2+1/2.

method.method_draft: Use a cross-section/45-45-90 triangle argument without coordinates. From the final picture, the contact points are the two upper inner corners of the adjoining unit squares, so they lie 1 inch above the base line and are 1 inch apart horizontally. How many inches is point $B$ from the line on which the bases of the original squares were placed?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The left side of the figure shows three side-by-side one-inch squares, whose bottom sides are all on the same horizontal straight line; the middle square is marked with shading, and point B is near the upper side of the middle square. The arrow indicates that the middle square is taken out and rotated 45°. The right side shows the rotated gray square in the shape of a rhombus, centered and put back in the original middle position, and lowered until it touches the upper inner corners of the two adjacent squares on the left and right; point B is the highest vertex of the rotated rhombus.

Reasoning: By the coordinate method, let the straight line where the bottom sides of the original three squares lie be y=0, and let the middle position be 1≤x≤2, so the center of the rotated square is on the line x=3/2. The upper inner corners of the left and right adjacent unit squares are respectively (1,1) and (2,1). Let the center of the rotated unit square be (3/2,c). After the unit square is rotated 45°, its diagonals are vertical and horizontal, and the half-diagonal length is r=√2/2. Therefore the bottom vertex is (3/2,c-r), and vertex B is (3/2,c+r). The left contact point (1,1) is on the lower-left side of the rhombus; this side has slope -1 and passes through the bottom vertex (3/2,c-r). Its equation satisfies y-(c-r)=-(x-3/2). Substitute (1,1): 1-(c-r)=-(1-3/2)=1/2, so c-r=1/2, that is, c=1/2+√2/2. Thus the height of point B is c+r=1/2+√2/2+√2/2=√2+1/2.
